description: Facts about the user's company, Larderly (fictional): metrics, team, product, customers, fundraising and policies, as the knowledge base stores them (#65). Several documents are near-duplicates on purpose (metrics for different months, two pricing pages) so only the precise one counts.

documents.title: What Larderly does
documents.text: Larderly is an inventory and food-cost app for independent restaurants. Kitchen staff photograph supplier invoices, Larderly reads every line item, and it tracks what each plate actually costs as ingredient prices move.

documents.title: Founding
documents.text: Larderly was founded in March 2025 in Oakland by Jordan Hale and Priya Raman. Jordan ran the back office of a family restaurant for six years; Priya was a staff engineer on a payments team.

documents.title: Mission
documents.text: Our mission: give a 12-seat neighborhood restaurant the same margin visibility a 300-location chain gets from its finance team.

documents.title: MRR June 2026
documents.text: Monthly recurring revenue at the end of June 2026 was $9,800 from 27 paying restaurants.

documents.title: MRR July 2026
documents.text: Monthly recurring revenue at the end of July 2026 was $11,600 from 32 paying restaurants.

documents.title: MRR August 2026
documents.text: Monthly recurring revenue at the end of August 2026 was $14,200 from 38 paying restaurants, up 22% month over month.

documents.title: Churn
documents.text: Logo churn has been two restaurants in the last six months: one closed for good, and one was bought by a group that uses a different system. No customer has left because of the product.

documents.title: Pricing
documents.text: Pricing is $29 per location per month for Basic, which covers invoice scanning and price alerts, and $149 per location per month for Pro, which adds recipe costing, menu engineering and POS sync.

documents.title: Pricing history
documents.text: Before May 2026 we charged a flat $99 per month. Moving to two tiers raised average revenue per restaurant from $99 to $374 because most customers chose Pro.

documents.title: Free trial
documents.text: New restaurants get a 21-day free trial with no card required. Trial-to-paid conversion has been 41% since we added the onboarding call.

documents.title: Team
documents.text: The team is four people: Jordan Hale (CEO), Priya Raman (CTO), Tomás Ferreira (founding engineer, joined January 2026) and Ines Kowal (contract product designer, three days a week).

documents.title: Advisor
documents.text: Dana Whitfield, who ran operations for a 40-location bakery group, advises Larderly for 0.25% vesting over two years. She meets Jordan every other Thursday.

documents.title: Pre-seed round
documents.text: Larderly raised a $750,000 pre-seed in September 2025 on a post-money SAFE with an $8M cap. Northgate Ventures led with $400,000; the rest came from six angels.

documents.title: Runway
documents.text: We have about $410,000 in the bank and burn roughly $31,000 a month, which gives us about 13 months of runway at the current headcount.

documents.title: Lead investor contact
documents.text: Our partner at Northgate Ventures is Marcus Lee. He prefers a short written update on the first Monday of each month rather than calls.

documents.title: Invoice OCR pipeline
documents.text: Invoice capture runs on the phone: the camera finds the page edges, on-device text recognition reads it, and a server model maps each line to a canonical ingredient. Accuracy on line items is 97.4% on our labelled set of 2,000 invoices.

documents.title: Tech stack
documents.text: The iOS app is Swift and SwiftUI. The backend is Go on Postgres, deployed on Fly.io. Priya chose Go because the team already knew it and it keeps the server cheap.

documents.title: POS integrations
documents.text: Larderly syncs sales from Toast and Square, so recipe costs can be multiplied by what was actually sold each night. Clover is next on the integration list.

documents.title: Biggest customer
documents.text: Our largest account is Casa Verde, a three-location Mexican restaurant group in Oakland and Berkeley on the Pro plan, paying $447 a month.

documents.title: First customer
documents.text: The first paying customer was Little Fern, a 24-seat cafe in Temescal. The owner, Rosa, signed up after Jordan helped her untangle a dairy invoice in person.

documents.title: Customer outcome
documents.text: Casa Verde found that their carnitas plate cost had drifted from 28% to 36% of the menu price after a pork price rise. They repriced and recovered about $2,100 a month.

documents.title: Ideal customer profile
documents.text: The ideal customer is an independent, owner-operated restaurant with one to five locations, $1M to $5M in annual sales, and no dedicated finance person.

documents.title: Go-to-market
documents.text: Most customers come from referrals and from Jordan walking into restaurants between 2 and 5 pm, when kitchens are quiet. Paid ads have not worked: the one test cost $640 per trial.

documents.title: Competitors
documents.text: The incumbents in back-office restaurant software sell to multi-unit groups, with onboarding that takes weeks and pricing in the hundreds per location. Spreadsheets and paper are the real competition for single locations.

documents.title: Differentiation
documents.text: Larderly is set up in under an hour with just a phone, works without a dedicated bookkeeper, and starts with the invoices a kitchen already has instead of asking staff to count inventory.

documents.title: Market size
documents.text: There are roughly 650,000 restaurant locations in the US and about 60% are independent. At $1,800 a year per location, independent restaurants alone are a market of about $700M a year.

documents.title: Roadmap Q4 2026
documents.text: Q4 2026 roadmap: Clover integration, supplier price comparisons across nearby restaurants (opt-in and anonymized), and a weekly margin summary sent by text message.

documents.title: Roadmap 2027
documents.text: In 2027 we plan to add ordering, so restaurants can reorder from suppliers inside Larderly, which would let us take a small payment fee on purchasing volume.

documents.title: Data policy
documents.text: Customer invoice images are deleted from our servers 90 days after processing. Only the extracted line items are kept, and customers can export or delete them at any time.

documents.title: Security
documents.text: Larderly encrypts data at rest and in transit, uses single sign-on for staff tools, and completed a third-party penetration test in July 2026 with no critical findings.

documents.title: Office
documents.text: We work from a shared studio above a bakery on Telegraph Avenue in Oakland. Rent is $1,900 a month and the lease runs until June 2027.

documents.title: Hiring plan
documents.text: The next two hires are a customer success lead who has worked in restaurants and a second iOS engineer. Both depend on raising the seed round.

documents.title: Seed round plan
documents.text: We plan to raise a $3M seed in early 2027 to reach 300 paying restaurants and $1.3M ARR within 18 months.

documents.title: Equity split
documents.text: Jordan and Priya each own 42% of Larderly after the pre-seed. The option pool is 10% and Tomás holds a 1.5% grant on a four-year vest.

documents.title: Net revenue retention
documents.text: Net revenue retention over the last six months is 128%, mostly from Basic customers upgrading to Pro and groups adding locations.

documents.title: Gross margin
documents.text: Gross margin is about 81%. The biggest cost of revenue is the server-side model that maps invoice lines to ingredients, at about 9 cents per invoice.

documents.title: Support hours
documents.text: Support runs by text message from 7 am to 11 pm Pacific, seven days a week, because restaurants work evenings and weekends. Median first response time is 6 minutes.

documents.title: Weekly metrics meeting
documents.text: Every Monday at 9 am the team reviews MRR, new trials, activation and support volume in a 30-minute meeting. Priya owns the dashboard.

documents.title: Activation metric
documents.text: We count a restaurant as activated once it has scanned ten invoices and costed five recipes. Activated restaurants convert to paid at 78%.

documents.title: Biggest risk
documents.text: The biggest risk is that restaurants churn when they go out of business, which happens to a lot of independents. We try to reduce it by selling to places that have been open more than two years.

documents.title: Brand
documents.text: Larderly's brand color is a deep tomato red and the logo is a lowercase l drawn as a ladle. Ines designed both in February 2026.

documents.title: Legal entity
documents.text: Larderly, Inc. is a Delaware C corporation incorporated on April 2, 2025. Our lawyer is at a small startup firm in San Francisco and our accountant is Pilot.

documents.title: Bank
documents.text: The company banks with Mercury and keeps reserves in a treasury account. The credit card limit is $25,000.

documents.title: Supplier relationships
documents.text: We have a data partnership with Bay Produce Co-op, which sends us their price list every morning, so Larderly can flag when a restaurant is paying more than the co-op rate.

documents.title: Customer quote
documents.text: Rosa from Little Fern said: 'I used to find out my costs went up when my accountant called in April. Now my phone tells me the day the invoice comes in.'

documents.title: Android
documents.text: There is no Android app yet. About 30% of kitchen staff use Android, so managers scan invoices on the owner's iPhone. An Android version is planned after the seed.

documents.title: Menu engineering feature
documents.text: Menu engineering sorts every dish into stars, plowhorses, puzzles and dogs by popularity and margin, using the POS sales data, and suggests which dishes to reprice or drop.

documents.title: Price alerts
documents.text: A price alert fires when an ingredient's unit price rises more than 8% against its 30-day average. Restaurants can change the threshold per ingredient.

documents.title: Board
documents.text: There is no formal board yet. Jordan and Priya are the two directors, and Marcus Lee from Northgate has board observer rights.

documents.title: Company values
documents.text: Values: be in the kitchen (talk to restaurants every week), ship small and often, and never make a restaurant feel stupid about their numbers.

documents.title: Engineering process
documents.text: We ship the iOS app every two weeks through TestFlight to five pilot restaurants first. Server changes deploy continuously behind feature flags.

documents.title: Accounting integration
documents.text: Larderly exports cost of goods sold to QuickBooks Online and Xero as journal entries at the end of each week, so the restaurant's books match what the kitchen spent.

documents.title: Waste tracking
documents.text: Pro customers can log waste with a photo and a reason, such as spoiled, dropped or over-prepped. Casa Verde cut produce waste by 18% in the first two months.

documents.title: Pilot program
documents.text: The five pilot restaurants that get early builds are Little Fern, Casa Verde, Hollow Pine Diner, Saffron Lane and Kettle & Crumb. They get Pro free in exchange for weekly feedback calls.

documents.title: Customer count by city
documents.text: Of 38 paying restaurants, 22 are in Oakland, 9 in Berkeley, 5 in San Francisco and 2 in Alameda.
